d.t: (obsolete, in the plural) A woman's period; menstrual discharge.
comparative degree of many: in greater number. (Used for a discrete quantity.)
d.e: There are more ways to do this than I can count.

d.t: comparative degree of much: in greater quantity, amount, or proportion. (Used for a continuous quantity.)
d.e: There's more caffeine in my coffee than in the coffee you get in most places.

d.t: Additional; further.
d.e: If you run out, there are more bandages in the first aid cupboard.

d.t: Bigger, stronger, or more valuable.
d.e: He is more than the ten years he spent behind bars at our local prison, as he is a changed man and his past does not define him.

d.t: To a greater degree or extent.
d.e: I like cake, but I like chocolate more.

d.t: Used to form the comparative form of adjectives and adverbs.
d.e: You're a great deal more beautiful than I ever imagined.

d.t: (now poetic) In negative constructions: any further, any longer; any more.
(now dialectal, humorous or proscribed) Used in addition to an inflected comparative form.
d.e: I was more better at English than you.

d.t: A greater number or quantity (of something).
d.e: We’re running out of napkins. I should have bought more.

d.t: An extra or additional quantity (of something).
d.e: There aren’t many people here yet, but more should be arriving soon.

d.t: comparative degree of many: in greater number. (Used for a discrete quantity.)
d.e: Last year’s applications received from new and returning students were more than each of the previous four years.

d.t: comparative degree of much: in greater quantity, amount, or proportion. (Used for a continuous quantity.)
(obsolete) A carrot; a parsnip.
(dialectal) A root; stock.
(dialectal) A plant; flower; shrub.

The early part of the day, especially from midnight to noon.
d.e: I'll see you tomorrow morning.

d.t: (figurative) The early part of anything.
(obsolete) That part of the day from dawn until the main meal (typically in late afternoon).
d.e: We breakfasted before nine, and do not dine till half-past six on the occasion, so I hope we three shall have a long morning enough.

d.t: (chiefly Scotland) The first alcoholic drink of the day; a morning draught.
Ellipsis of good morning.
superlative degree of much.
d.e: The teams competed to see who could collect (the) most money.

d.t: superlative degree of many: the comparatively largest number of (construed with the definite article)
d.e: The team with the most points wins.

d.t: superlative degree of many: the majority of; more than half of (construed without the definite article)
d.e: Most bakers and dairy farmers have to get up early.

d.t: Forms the superlative of many adjectives.
d.e: This is the most important example.

d.t: To a great extent or degree; highly; very.
d.e: This is a most unusual specimen.

d.t: superlative degree of much
(informal, chiefly US) Clipping of almost.
(slang, dated) The greatest; the best.
The greater part of a group, especially a group of people.
d.e: Most want the best for their children.

d.t: (uncountable) The greatest amount.
d.e: The most I can offer for the house is $150,000.

d.t: (countable, uncountable) The greater part.
d.e: Most of the penguins were friendly and curious.

d.t: (countable) A record-setting amount.
A female parent, especially of a human; a female who parents a child (which she has given birth to, adopted, fostered, etc).
d.e: I am visiting my mother any moment.

d.t: A pregnant female; mother-to-be; a female who gestates a baby.
d.e: Nutrients and oxygen obtained by the mother are conveyed to the fetus.

d.t: A female who donates a fertilized egg or donates a body cell which has resulted in a clone.
(figuratively) A female ancestor.
(figuratively) A source or origin.
d.e: Near-synonym: matrix

d.t: Something that is the greatest or most significant of its kind. (See mother of all.)
d.e: Near-synonym: Big One

d.t: (dated, when followed by a surname) A title of respect for one's mother-in-law.
d.e: Mother Smith, meet my cousin, Doug Jones.

d.t: (dated) A term of address for one's wife.
(figuratively) Any elderly woman, especially within a particular community.
d.e: Near-synonyms: matron, matriarch

d.t: (figuratively) Any person or entity which performs mothering.
d.e:
Judges 5:7, KJV.
The inhabitants of the villages ceased, they ceased in Israel, until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel.

d.t: Dregs, lees; a stringy, mucilaginous or film- or membrane-like substance (consisting of a culture of acetobacters) which develops in fermenting alcoholic liquids (such as wine, or cider), and turns the alcohol into acetic acid with the help of oxygen from the air.
d.e: pieces of mother ;   adding mother to vinegar

d.e: mothered oil, mothered vinegar, mothered wine

d.t: (intransitive, of an alcohol) To develop mother.

A mother-in-law apartment.

d.t: (intransitive) To act; to take action; to begin to act
d.e: to move in a matter

d.t: (intransitive) To change residence, for example from one house, town, or state, to another; to go and live at another place; similarly to change the location of another establishment such as a business. See also move out and move in.
d.e: I decided to move to the country for a more peaceful life.

d.t: (transitive) To transport (an item) as part of changing residences.
d.e: Before my lease ended, I gave away my old sofa because I didn't want to move it.

d.t: (transitive, ergative) To cause to change place or posture in any manner; to set in motion; to carry, convey, draw, or push from one place to another
d.e: The waves moved the boat up and down.

d.t: (transitive, chess, board games) To transfer (a piece) from one space or position on the board to another.
d.e: She moved the queen closer to the centre of the board.

d.t: (transitive) To excite to action by the presentation of motives; to rouse by representation, persuasion, or appeal; to influence.
d.e: This song moves me to dance.

d.t: (transitive) To arouse the feelings or passions of; especially, to excite to tenderness or compassion, to excite (for example, an emotion).
d.e: That book really moved me.

d.t: (transitive, intransitive) To propose; to recommend; specifically, to propose formally for consideration and determination, in a deliberative assembly; to submit
d.e: I move to repeal the rule regarding obligatory school uniform.

d.t: (transitive, obsolete) To mention; to raise (a question); to suggest (a course of action); to lodge (a complaint).
(transitive, obsolete) To incite, urge (someone to do something); to solicit (someone for or of an issue); to make a proposal to.
(transitive, obsolete) To apply to, as for aid.
The act of moving; a movement.
d.e: A slight move of the tiller, and the boat will go off course.

d.t: An act for the attainment of an object; a step in the execution of a plan or purpose.
d.e: He made another move towards becoming a naturalized citizen.

d.t: A formalized or practiced action used in athletics, dance, physical exercise, self-defense, hand-to-hand combat, etc.
d.e: She always gets spontaneous applause for that one move.

d.t: The event of changing one's residence.
d.e: The move into my fiancé's house took two long days.

d.t: A change in strategy.
d.e: I am worried about our boss's move.

d.t: A transfer, a change from one employer to another.
(board games) The act of moving a token on a gameboard from one position to another according to the rules of the game.
d.e: The best move of the game was when he sacrificed his rook in order to gain better possession.

d.t: (board games, usually in the plural) A round, in which each player has a turn.
d.e: You can win in three moves if you do that.

d.t: (syntax) Within the Minimalist Program, a fundamental operation of syntactic construction
(idiomatic, intransitive) To continue; to proceed; to go on.
d.e: After spending the night resting in an abandoned church, the group decided to move on in their quest.

d.t: (idiomatic, intransitive) To start dealing with something else.
d.e: The best revenge is always to just happily move on and let karma do the rest.

d.t: (idiomatic, transitive, informal) To attempt a seduction, often in a way seen as disloyal or rude to another.
d.e: I think Shane is going to move on my ex tonight.

d.t: To physically move something or someone.
d.e: The police moved the protestors on.

d.t: (African-American Vernacular, transitive) To assault or attack.
A large amount of.

d.t: (in combinations such as 'as much', 'this much') Used to indicate, demonstrate or compare the quantity of something.

d.t: (now archaic or nonstandard) A great number of; many (people).
(now Caribbean, African-American, UK regional) many ( + plural countable noun).
(obsolete) Large, great.
(obsolete) Long in duration.
To a great extent.

d.t: Often; frequently.
d.e: Does he get drunk much?

d.t: (in combinations such as 'as much', 'this much') Used to indicate or compare extent.
d.e: I don't like Wagner as much as I like Mozart.

d.t: (slang) Combining with an adjective or (occasionally) a noun, used in a rhetorical question to mock someone for having the specified quality.

d.t: (obsolete) Almost.
A large amount or great extent; a lot.

d.t: A series of sounds organized in time, usually employing some combination of harmony, melody, rhythm, tempo, timbre, sound design, lyrics, etc., often to convey a mood.
d.e: I keep listening to this music because it’s a masterpiece.

d.t: (figuratively) Any interesting or pleasing sounds.
An art form, created by organizing pitch, rhythm, and sounds made using musical instruments and/or singing.
A guide to playing or singing a particular tune; sheet music.
(military, slang) Electronic signal jamming.
(US, slang, dated) Heated argument.
(US, slang, dated) Fun; amusement.

To do as a requirement; indicates that the sentence subject is required as an imperative or directive to execute the sentence predicate, with failure to do so resulting in a failure or negative consequence.
d.e: You must arrive in class on time.

d.t: To do with certainty; indicates that the speaker is certain that the subject will have executed the predicate.
d.e: If it has rained all day, it must be very wet outside.

d.t: Used to indicate that something is very likely, probable, or certain to be true.
d.e: The children must be asleep by now.
